events.reason: Total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (100 mcg) by mouth daily on an empty stomach

conditions.label: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
conditions.note: s/p total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection 1/22/2026; 1.7 cm right lobe, margins negative, 0/9 central nodes

reports.text:
SPECIMENS: (A) total thyroidectomy, stitch marks superior right; (B) central (level VI) lymph nodes.
GROSS: (A) thyroid gland, oriented; a 1.7 cm firm tan-white nodule in the right lobe. Left lobe and isthmus without gross lesion. (B) fibrofatty tissue with nine lymph nodes.
MICROSCOPIC: (A) medullary thyroid carcinoma composed of nests and sheets of round to spindled cells in a stroma with amyloid. Surgical margins free of carcinoma. Left lobe and isthmus: benign thyroid tissue. No parathyroid tissue in the specimen. (B) nine lymph nodes, all negative for carcinoma.
reports.conclusion: Thyroid, total thyroidectomy: MEDULLARY THYROID CARCINOMA, 1.7 cm, right lobe; margins negative. Central neck lymph nodes: 0 of 9 involved.

documents.title: Operative Report - Total Thyroidectomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT (received 01/27/2026)
Date of surgery: 01/22/2026
Preoperative diagnosis: suspected medullary thyroid carcinoma, right thyroid nodule; MEN 2A (RET p.Cys634Arg); status post right adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma 11/14/2025.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: total thyroidectomy with bilateral central (level VI) neck dissection.
Anesthesia: general, with recurrent laryngeal nerve monitoring.

Description: Transverse collar incision in a skin crease. Strap muscles separated in the midline. The right lobe was mobilized; the right recurrent laryngeal nerve was identified and preserved with intact signal. Both right parathyroid glands were identified and preserved on their blood supply. The same was done on the left, with the left recurrent laryngeal nerve and both left parathyroid glands identified and preserved. Total thyroidectomy completed. Central compartment lymph node dissection performed bilaterally. Hemostasis. Layered closure.
Findings: firm nodule in the right lobe. Nerve signal intact bilaterally at the end of the case.
EBL: minimal. Complications: none.
Disposition: overnight observation with calcium check in the morning.

General Surgery

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 01/27/2026)
Admitted 01/22/2026 - discharged 01/23/2026.
Procedure: total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection, 01/22/2026.

Course: Uncomplicated. Voice normal postoperatively. No numbness, tingling or cramping. Morning calcium on 01/23 normal (9.6 mg/dL); no calcium supplement needed. Tolerating diet, pain controlled. Incision clean and dry.
Pathology pending at discharge.

Discharge medications: NEW levothyroxine 100 mcg by mouth once daily on an empty stomach.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: surgical clinic 2 weeks; primary care within 2 weeks; TSH about 6 weeks after surgery; endocrinology for postoperative calcitonin and CEA in about 3 months.
Return precautions: neck swelling, trouble breathing, tingling around the mouth or in the fingers, muscle cramps.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call - discharged 1/23 after total thyroidectomy; discharge records received this morning. Voice sounds normal to me on the phone. No tingling in lips or fingers, no cramps. Neck incision a little stiff, no swelling. Taking levothyroxine 100 mcg every morning before breakfast - reviewed separating it from coffee and any calcium or iron by 30-60 min. Appt with PCP 2/3 at 11:00.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit (TCM)
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital: 1/22-1/23, total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection.
Path (final 1/27): medullary thyroid carcinoma, 1.7 cm, right lobe, margins negative, 0 of 9 central nodes. Parathyroids identified and preserved at surgery.
Discharge med: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily (new).

S: Recovering well. Voice normal, no hoarseness. No tingling or cramps. Swallowing fine. Diarrhea is settling - fewer loose stools than before the operation. Taking levothyroxine correctly in the morning. Still no spells since the adrenal surgery. Plans to go back to school next week.

O: BP 120/66, HR 75 /min, RR 17 /min, SpO2 96 %, T 36.7 C, Wt 64.9 kg
Neck: collar incision healing well, no erythema, swelling or fluid collection. Voice clear.
Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen: healed port sites.
Chvostek negative.

Labs today (resulted this afternoon): BMP normal, calcium 9.7 mg/dL.

A/P
1. MTC, s/p total thyroidectomy + CND 1/22/26 - favorable path. Endocrinology to follow calcitonin and CEA; their visit is booked for April.
2. Post-thyroidectomy on levothyroxine 100 mcg - TSH in early March.
3. Calcium normal, no supplement needed.
4. Diarrhea improving.
5. Pheochromocytoma s/p R adrenalectomy - BP normal off meds.
6. MEN 2A - surveillance per endocrinology.
Cleared to return to work 2/9. RTC for annual in summer.

events.reason: Follow-up after thyroidectomy, calcitonin and CEA

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date: 04/23/2026

Ms. Friedman returns three months after total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection (01/22/2026) for medullary thyroid carcinoma, MEN 2A (RET p.Cys634Arg). Right adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma 11/14/2025; plasma free metanephrines normal 12/18/2025.

Interval: Feeling well. The diarrhea has resolved completely. No spells. Voice normal. Taking levothyroxine 100 mcg daily; TSH in range in March.

Exam: BP 109/71, HR 79 /min, Wt 63.8 kg. Well-healed collar incision; no palpable neck mass or adenopathy.

Pathology reviewed: MTC 1.7 cm, right lobe, margins negative, 0/9 central nodes.

Labs (04/23/2026)
Calcitonin: undetectable, <2 pg/mL
CEA: 2.1 ng/mL

Assessment
1. Medullary thyroid carcinoma, status post total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection: postoperative calcitonin undetectable and CEA normal, an excellent biochemical response.
2. MEN 2A, pheochromocytoma status post right adrenalectomy.
3. Post-thyroidectomy, on levothyroxine.

Plan
- Repeat calcitonin and CEA in six months.
- First yearly plasma free metanephrines drawn the same day.
- Continue levothyroxine 100 mcg daily; TSH per primary care.
- Next visit booked: 10/22/2026.

Endocrinology
